findings.claim: blast_radius `reading` is computed only from OWNED files: an empty change set reads `contained`, and a change where most files are unowned (map-blind) still reads contained/local with no qualifier.

(b) `blast_radius {files: [apps/api/models/recipe.py, apps/web/src/app/App.tsx, scripts/foo.py]}` → 2 of 3 files in `unowned_files`, `reading: "local"` — the reading ignores the two blind files (gastify's file census is 50 claimed / 44 unclaimed, so mixed sets are the common case).

findings.claim: who_calls direction=out reuses the callers-arm delta semantics: grep hits are USAGES (callers) of the symbol, but two_arm computes missed = grep code files − callees − defs, so the symbol's known callers are reported as 'missed_by_map', and reach/reach_line mix callees into the Reach record form.

The agent concludes the index missed a caller it actually knows; reach_line '- **Reach:** apps/api/api/account.py · apps/api/services/account_export.py (graft@50f9aac7)' presents callees as reach.
findings.evidence: y_wc_out_cross.json vs y_wc_in_cross.json (gustify); mapquery.py:425 `missed = [p for p in code_files if p not in callers and p not in defs]` with callers = graft --direction out hits; tools.py:466-471 only renames callers→callees and adds an emit_skipped note.
findings.fix: When direction=='out' or depth!='1': set missed_by_map=[] with a note ('grep finds callers; not comparable to callees/transitive'), and set reach_line=null (record form is callers-only); keep grep_code_files as 'usages'.

findings.claim: graft 0.8.2 exits 1 for an unknown symbol ('✗ no symbol … in the graph'); graft_callers maps every rc≠0 to callers_status 'unavailable: graft exit 1 […]', so on real twins the spec'd `map_claim: absent: symbol not in the graft index` never appears and an unindexed symbol is indistinguishable from a broken binary/index.

findings.claim: classify_hit treats a symbol inside f-string literal text as CODE on Python 3.12, so a log/format line that merely names a function becomes a 'missed caller' and — with a map claim present — a FALSE map-delta is written to .kdbp/map-deltas.jsonl.
findings.failure_scenario: gustify (emits disabled): who_calls TaxonomyDimension → map_claim present, missed_by_map includes scripts/gen_taxonomy.py whose only two occurrences are string text (L157 plain string → prose, correct; L207 `lines.append(f"export const {const}: TaxonomyDimension = {{\n")` → shape code, code_hits 1). With emit on and the kdbp/ignore gates open, the server appends `_a3_graft.calls callers(TaxonomyDimension) scripts/gen_taxonomy.py:207` — a delta for a non-call; /gabe-commit tallies it and pulse S14 nags a generator miss that does not exist. 13 gustify files name a mapped symbol ONLY inside f-string text (coverage · complete · verify · Recipe · complexity · register · TaxonomyDimension).
findings.evidence: mapquery.py:358-359 keeps spans only for `t.type in (tokenize.COMMENT, tokenize.STRING)`. Under 3.12 (`python3 --version` 3.12.3) tokenize emits FSTRING_START/FSTRING_MIDDLE/FSTRING_END for f-strings — probe: `log.info(f"apply_filters done for {x}")` → 'code', token list shows `FSTRING_MIDDLE 'apply_filters done for '`; `rf"apply_filters\d"` → 'code'; the plain `"apply_filters %s" % x` → 'prose'. Client run on gustify reproduced the missed_by_map entry above. The battery fixture has no f-string case, so the pin is silent.
findings.fix: Add the f-string middle token to the span filter: `_PROSE_TOK = {tokenize.COMMENT, tokenize.STRING} | {t for t in (getattr(tokenize, n, None) for n in ('FSTRING_MIDDLE', 'TSTRING_MIDDLE')) if t}` and use `t.type in _PROSE_TOK` at L359 (FSTRING_START/END cannot contain the symbol). Battery: add a fixture file whose only mention is `log.info(f"thing done")` and assert it lands in grep_prose_files with 0 emits.

findings.claim: freshness reports 'uncommitted regen — archmap.json is modified in the worktree' on a CLEAN tree whenever the committed archmap's `head` is not an ancestor of the commit that landed it (map regenerated on another branch, merged/cherry-picked), because base falls back to that off-branch head and dirty_map is read from the base-vs-worktree diff instead of git status.
findings.failure_scenario: Scratch clone of gastify checked out at 262ac069 (a real commit; `git status --porcelain` empty): freshness → {head 7d76d515, base 7d76d515, stale null, freshness 'uncommitted regen', reason 'archmap.json is modified in the worktree'}. Every tool answer at that state stamps `map@7d76d515 · uncommitted regen`, telling the model there is a dirty regen to commit (there is none) while hiding the real fact — the map was generated on a branch this checkout never had. 4 of gastify's last 8 archmap commits (262ac069, b0acf426, 49bd8a63, a6ba1793) carry such an off-branch head, so this state has recurred on a live twin.
findings.evidence: mapquery.py:243-246: `merge-base --is-ancestor head cand` fails → `base = head`; L250 `git diff --name-only <base>` then diffs an unrelated tree against the worktree, listing docs/site/center/archmap.json; L261 `dirty_map = any(l.strip().endswith('archmap.json') for l in diff.splitlines())` reads that committed difference as a worktree modification. (L261's `rc` is also the rc of the `git status` call at L253, not the diff — harmless today.) Reproduction command: `git clone gastify <scratch>; git checkout 262ac069; python3 -c 'import mapquery as mq; c,_=mq.open_center(root); print(mq.freshness(c))'`.
findings.fix: Derive dirty_map from the porcelain status already fetched (`any(l[:2].strip() and l[3:].strip() == CENTER_REL + '/archmap.json' for l in st.splitlines())`), and when `cand` exists but does not descend from `head`, keep `base = cand` (the commit that introduced this map content) and answer `freshness: 'unknown', stale: None, reason: 'map head %s is not an ancestor of %s — regenerated on another branch; mapped_files_changed is measured since %s'`. Battery: fixture with a regen commit cherry-picked from a side branch, clean tree → freshness unknown and never 'uncommitted regen'.

findings.claim: The real graft (0.8.2) exits 1 for a symbol that is simply not indexed, so graft_callers labels the arm `unavailable: graft exit 1 [...]` instead of the spec'd `map_claim: absent: symbol not in the graft index`, and echoes graft's stderr — including the directive 'run graft build' — into the result; the battery's fake graft returns rc 0 with `matches: []`, so the pin exercises a behaviour the shipped binary does not have.
findings.failure_scenario: gustify: who_calls self / who_calls get_db → callers_status = `unavailable: graft exit 1 ['✗ no symbol "self" in the graph — check spelling or run graft build']`, map_claim = `absent: unavailable: …`. The model reads a broken arm (and a third-party instruction to run `graft build`, which D10 forbids surfacing) where the truth is 'not indexed'; reach_line degrades to grep-only correctly only by accident of the `startswith('absent: no index')` test.
findings.evidence: mapquery.py:319-320: `if rc != 0: return None, 'unavailable: graft exit %d %s' % (rc, (err or out).strip().splitlines()[:1])`. Client output on gustify quoted above. tests/gabe-map/checks.py fake_graft: `*) echo '{"query":…,"matches":[]}' ;;` (exit 0). map-spec.md §3: 'Unknown symbol in graft → map_claim: absent: symbol not in the graft index'; design §12.4 asked for exactly this rc-1 mapping.
findings.fix: In graft_callers: `if rc == 1 and 'no symbol' in (err or out): return '{"matches": []}', 'ran'` so parse_callers yields the spec'd claim; for other non-zero exits return `'unavailable: graft exit %d' % rc` and log the stderr (never return it). Battery: make the fake graft exit 1 with the real message for unknown symbols and assert `map_claim == 'absent: symbol not in the graft index'` and that 'graft build' appears in no result field.

findings.claim: find_center walks above the git toplevel, so a nested checkout without its own center (a worktree of a pre-center branch under <repo>/.claude/worktrees/, a vendored repo) is served the PARENT checkout's map as its own: `root` ≠ `center.root`, freshness describes the parent tree, grep/graft/.kdbp gates run on the nested tree, and every answer stamps present · fresh.
findings.failure_scenario: gastify clone, `git worktree add .claude/worktrees/old 6516722f^` (176 backend files, no docs/site/center): CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<worktree> → map_status = {present True, root <worktree>, center <clone>/docs/site/center, map 'map@7f78bcfe · fresh', graft index_present False}; who_calls useCardAliases greps the OLD tree and pairs it with the parent's map claims. The map is for a different tree; 'fresh' is computed on the parent checkout (`git -C center.root`), never on the tree the agent is editing. Claude Code's EnterWorktree places worktrees exactly there.
findings.evidence: resolve_root L89-90 normalizes to the nested repo's toplevel; find_center L96-99 iterates `(base, *base.parents)` with no repo boundary; Center.root (L107) = center's grandparent; freshness L227 uses center.root while two_arm/graft_callers/git_grep_hits/kdbp gate (tools.t_who_calls) use `root`. map-spec §3 states one root law ('the project root is the center's grandparent … every reused loader receives THAT root') that this path violates. Reproduced via the battery client with absolute paths.
findings.fix: Bound the walk at the repo: in find_center compute `top = git_toplevel(root)` and `break` when `top and not (str(d) == top or str(d).startswith(top + os.sep))` — or, in open_center, return `(None, 'nearest center %s belongs to a different checkout than %s' % (c, root))` when `project_root_of(c) != root and git_toplevel(root)`; keep the unbounded walk only for a root that is in no repo. Battery: a fixture worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` on a pre-center commit → present False with that reason.

findings.claim: The freshness 'mapped set' is entities[].files ∪ fe.pieces[].file only, so the test files test_insight was derived from (79 on gustify, 87 on gastify — all tracked) are never watched: adding/renaming cases in a test file leaves `stale:false` while cases_for/touches.tests keep answering from the stale insight with 'fresh' stamped.

Measured read-only on both twins: tfiles referenced by test_insight.by_function rows not in mapped = 79/79 (gustify), 87/87 (gastify); by_file keys are the mapped source, never the tests.

Battery: uncommitted edit to apps/api/tests/test_thing.py → not fresh.

findings.claim: _load_json catches JSONDecodeError and OSError but not UnicodeDecodeError, so a center file with one invalid UTF-8 byte makes EVERY tool call an isError crash (stamp → freshness → archmap) instead of the promised honest-empty.
findings.failure_scenario: archmap.json containing `"doc":"caf\xe9"` (a generator writing a latin-1 docstring without ensure_ascii) → `_load_json` raises UnicodeDecodeError; map_status/touches/who_calls all return `{error: 'UnicodeDecodeError: …'}` with isError true; the model gets no `present`/`reason`/hint.
findings.evidence: Probe: `_load_json(Path with b'{"head":"abc","doc":"caf\xe9"}')` → CRASH UnicodeDecodeError. L124-125 `except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError)`; UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError, not a JSONDecodeError.
findings.fix: `except (ValueError, OSError) as exc:` (JSONDecodeError is a ValueError subclass, so nothing is lost).

findings.claim: When a cached center file disappears, _load_json returns {} without evicting the cache entry, so Center.idx()'s key still matches and the OLD indexes are served alongside an empty archmap.
findings.failure_scenario: archmap.json removed from the worktree after a load (branch switch that drops it while center.config.json stays, or a regen that unlinks before rewriting): `entities()` → {} but `idx()['mapped_files']`/`file_owners`/`fn_by_bare` still answer from the deleted map — touches/owner_of report owners for a map that is not on disk, and freshness silently reads 'archmap carries no head' next to a populated index.
findings.evidence: Probe: after `archmap.json.unlink()`, `c.idx()['mapped_files']` = {'apps/x.py','apps/z.py',…} while `c.entities()` = {}. L116-118 return {} on FileNotFoundError leaving `_CACHE[str(path)]`; idx() L157-161 compares against that stale key.
findings.fix: On FileNotFoundError: `_CACHE.pop(str(path), None); return {}`.

findings.claim: `reach`, `callers`, `defs` and the joined `reach_line` are uncapped (D11 says every list is capped and named), and the record-form reach_line is also produced for direction=out / depth>1 queries where `reach` means callees ∪ transitive callers, not the phase's reach.
findings.failure_scenario: gustify who_calls self → reach 55 files, reach_line 2,281 chars, 18.8k-char result (~4.7k tokens) on a mid-size twin; a hot symbol with graft depth=all or a larger repo scales this toward the 25k-token result cap while `capped:true` refers only to missed/grep_hits. who_calls {symbol, direction:'out'} returns `- **Reach:** <callees…> (graft@sha)` — a PLAN.md-pasteable record whose files are callees.
findings.evidence: two_arm L449-452: `'callers': sorted(callers)`, `'defs': sorted(defs)`, `'reach': reach` with no cap; reach_line L462 joins all of `result['reach']`; tools.py t_who_calls L428 calls reach_line unconditionally. Measured through the client on gustify (numbers above).
findings.fix: Cap `callers`/`defs`/`reach` at CAP with `reach_more`/`callers_more` counts and extend `capped` to them; in reach_line, when `len(reach) > CAP` emit the first CAP + `… +N` and, in t_who_calls, set `reach_line` to `None` with a note when `direction != 'in' or depth != '1'`.

findings.claim: who_calls' emit gate (e) — 'the root is inside the session's roots (an explicit foreign root is read-only)', map-spec.md:117 — is OPEN whenever the session declares no roots: `allowed = [...] or None` (tools.py:458) hands mapquery.two_arm `allowed_roots=None`, which mapquery.py:428 defines as `root_allowed: True` for ANY root (the CLI 'no gate' meaning reach-emit.py:55 relies on).
findings.failure_scenario: A client that does not set CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and declares `capabilities: {}` (no roots — any non-Claude-Code MCP host) calls who_calls(symbol=Recipe, root=/some/other/project, emit=true). Reproduced on gustify with emits disabled: the reply carries `gates: {claim: present, kdbp: true, root_allowed: True}` and `emit_skipped: []`; with GABE_MAP_NO_EMIT unset the same call passes every gate and `emit_delta` appends to the FOREIGN project's .kdbp/map-deltas.jsonl (when it is gitignored there) — the one write the spec says an explicit foreign root can never cause. Under Claude Code the hole is closed only incidentally (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is always set, §2), so the reach is non-Claude-Code clients.
findings.evidence: tools.py:455-459 `allowed = list(roots or []); if CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: append; allowed = [toplevel...] or None; two_arm(..., allowed_roots=allowed)` · mapquery.py:428 `"root_allowed": True if allowed_roots is None else root in allowed_roots` · reach-emit.py:55 passes `allowed_roots=None` deliberately (CLI = no gate). Live run (attack.py §11, capabilities {}, no CPD, cwd=/tmp, root=gustify, GABE_MAP_NO_EMIT=1): gates.root_allowed=True, emit_skipped=[]. No battery case covers the no-roots path (grep root_allowed/allowed_roots in tests/ → none).
findings.fix: Never pass None from the MCP path — tools.py:458: `allowed = [mq.git_toplevel(p) or p for p in allowed] or ([root] if not args.get("root") else [])` (no session roots ⇒ only the default-resolved root may emit; an explicit root with nothing to check it against is read-only). Add a battery case in tests/gabe-map/checks.py: initialize with `capabilities: {}` + no CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR + explicit foreign root → `emit_skipped` names 'root outside the session roots (read-only)'.

findings.claim: Routing is by the presence of `id` alone, so a `notifications/*` message that (spec-violatingly) carries an `id` is dispatched to on_request, never on_notification; for `notifications/initialized` the server answers -32601 and `self.initialized` stays False for the life of the session.
findings.failure_scenario: Client sends `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":7,"method":"notifications/initialized"}` (a client that stamps ids on every frame). Reproduced live on both servers: reply -32601 'method not found (pre-initialize): notifications/initialized', then every subsequent tools/list and tools/call → -32602 'server not initialized' forever; the server never asks for roots either. Only a spec-violating client triggers it (the TS SDK never adds an id to notifications), hence low.
findings.evidence: mcpwire.py:179-184 `if "method" in msg and "id" in msg: on_request … elif "method" in msg: on_notification`; on_request:119-122 falls to the pre-initialize -32601 branch and never sets `initialized`. attack.py §1 output: '-32601 … notifications/initialized' followed by tools/list → -32602.
findings.fix: One line in handle_line before the request branch: `if str(msg.get("method", "")).startswith("notifications/"): return self.on_notification(msg)` — notifications are defined by their method namespace in MCP, and an id on one must be ignored, not answered.

findings.claim: A roots/list result whose `roots` is an EMPTY list is discarded (`if roots: self.roots = roots`), so after `notifications/roots/list_changed` the server keeps the previous roots instead of the authoritative new (empty) list.
findings.failure_scenario: Session starts with roots [/a]; the client later sends roots/list_changed and answers the server's re-request with `{"roots": []}`. Reproduced live (attack.py §10): the next tools/call still reports `root_source: roots/list` with the old root. Consequences: resolve_root keeps falling back to a root the client withdrew (instead of cwd), and who_calls' root_allowed gate keeps treating the withdrawn directory as an in-session root that may be emitted into. Marginal under Claude Code (roots never shrink to []), hence low.
findings.evidence: mcpwire.py:90-99: `roots = []; for r in ...; if roots: self.roots = roots` — the guard turns 'no file:// roots' into 'no change'. map-spec.md:29-30 treats the reply as the roots list, not as a delta.
findings.fix: Assign unconditionally when the reply is a result: replace `if roots:` with `self.roots = roots` (keep the log line), so an authoritative empty list clears the stored roots.

findings.claim: _table() terminates the row walk at the first non-`|` non-comment line (a blank line or a prose block), so any table with blank lines between row groups is silently truncated — both twins' PENDING files are.

findings.evidence: Live gastify kdbp_snapshot → pending {open:2, closed:13}; pending_row_preview → next_id 16. `awk` over gastify PENDING.md: 185 rows, blank lines at 25,37,39,43,50,58,…,218, prose `## 2026-06-30 — [LOW / defer] …` at 219, rows P128–P186 resume at 225–325. gustify: `awk 'NR>42 && NR<135 && !/^\|/'` → blank at 70 and 134; rows before the blank = 24 of 87. Code: kdbp_tools.py:65–68 — `if l2.lstrip().startswith('<!--'): continue` / `if not l2.startswith('|'): break`.
findings.fix: In _table() skip blank lines (`if not l2.strip(): continue`) and, rather than breaking on any other non-`|` line, stop only when a NEW table header+separator pair begins (or EOF), skipping intervening prose; keep the comment skip. findings.fix: At mapquery.py:309 add `if not SYMBOL_RE.match(sym): return None, "unavailable: symbol is not an identifier"` (defense in depth for every caller); in reach-emit.py:114 use `r"\b%s\b" % re.escape(s)` and reject non-identifier symbols with a usage error.

findings.claim: `json` is never imported in tools.py, so `_map_confidence` raises NameError the moment a project has a map-delta rollup ledger — `who_calls` returns isError instead of an answer.
findings.failure_scenario: Any project where `/gabe-commit`'s sweep has written `.kdbp/map-deltas-rollup.jsonl` with ≥1 line (the intended steady state of the map-delta loop). `mcp__gabe-map__who_calls {"symbol":"thing"}` → `isError:true`, body `{"tool":"who_calls","error":"NameError: name 'json' is not defined"}`. The whole answer is lost — callers, grep arms, reach_line, and the emit report — even though `two_arm` (tools.py:459) has already run and, on a project with a graft index, already appended the delta line before the crash at :472.
findings.evidence: tools.py imports at :9-14 are `hashlib, os, re, sys, pathlib.Path` only — no `json`; :425 `o = json.loads(line)` and :426 `except json.JSONDecodeError`. Both raise NameError, and the enclosing `except OSError` at :433 does not catch it. Reproduced end-to-end against the battery's own fixture repo plus a one-line rollup file: `client.py … call who_calls '{"symbol":"thing"}'` → `[isError] {"tool":"who_calls","error":"NameError: name 'json' is not defined"}`. Battery blind spot: tests/gabe-map/checks.py:405 only pins the no-ledger branch ("no map-delta ledger → honest"); no fixture ever creates the rollup file, and no test forces any tool-body exception, so map-spec §2's "a tool-body exception → isError:true" law is itself unpinned.
findings.fix: Add `import json` to tools.py's import block (:10-13). Then pin it: seed `.kdbp/map-deltas-rollup.jsonl` in the fixture and assert `map_confidence.active_missed_edges == 1` on a fresh tally and `0` past the `MAP_DELTAS_H` horizon.

findings.claim: `_table` returns the FIRST markdown table whose header contains the keyword, so on gustify every PENDING tool reads the 7-row "Production-gate map" index instead of the 24-row canonical `## Rows` table.
findings.failure_scenario: On gustify (a propagation target), `mcp__gabe-kdbp__kdbp_snapshot` reports `pending: {open: 7, closed: 0, columns: ['#','Gate','Finding']}` — the gate-map summary at PENDING.md:32 — while the real deferral table at PENDING.md:44 (11-column canon, 24 open rows) is never read. Worse, `pending_row_preview` mints `next_id` over that decoy table and returns `"row": "| #208 | review | [test] probe only |"` with `columns: ['#','Gate','Finding']`. An agent pasting that 3-cell row into the 11-column `## Rows` table produces exactly the malformed-row/cell-shift defect gustify's own PENDING #137 was opened about.
findings.evidence: kdbp_tools.py:56-71 `_table` breaks out of the scan on the first `|`-line containing the keyword. gustify/.kdbp/PENDING.md:32 is `| # | Gate | Finding |` (7 rows, no Status/Priority columns) and :44 is `| # | Date | Source | Finding | File | Scale | Priority | Impact | Times Deferred | Status | Verified |` (24 rows). Live run against the twin, read-only: snapshot `open 7 / closed 0`; `pending_row_preview` → `| #208 | review | [test] probe only |`. The commit message records this same output as an expected result ("gustify's 3 columns"), so the smoke test read the decoy as the real table. Both battery fixtures (tests/gabe-kdbp/checks.py make_repo + make_variant) contain exactly ONE table per file, so multi-table ambiguity is UNPINNED.
findings.fix: In `_table`, among all candidate header lines choose the one with the most header cells (ties → first) instead of the first match. Prototyped on a copy: gustify then reports `open 24 / columns [#,Date,Source,Finding,File,Scale,Priority,Impact,Times Deferred,Status,Verified]`, gastify is unchanged, and tests/gabe-kdbp stays 38/38. Add a fixture PENDING.md with a decoy summary table above the canon table.

findings.claim: `_table` never checks that the matched line is actually a header (no `|---|` separator on the next line), so a DATA row containing the keyword is parsed as a table header — gastify's headerless LEDGER is reported as structured rows.
findings.failure_scenario: gastify's `.kdbp/LEDGER.md` has no table header and no separator row anywhere. `mcp__gabe-kdbp__kdbp_snapshot` matches LEDGER.md:7369 — a PUSH data row whose Gates text contains the words "dirty entry" — as the header, then reports `ledger.last[0] = {date:'', entry:'<700-char GS6 commit blurb>', theme:'', commits:'', gates:'', line:7371}`. An agent asking "what were the last beats here" is handed fabricated structure. The same garbage feeds `review_target` (kdbp_tools.py:330 `ledger_rows(led, 400)` → :334 theme/entry phase matching), so on any project with a headerless or prose LEDGER the phase→commits resolution silently mis-resolves instead of falling back.
findings.evidence: kdbp_tools.py:60 matches on `ln.startswith("|") and header_must_have.lower() in ln.lower()` with no separator validation; :63-69 then treats lines from i+2 onward as rows. `grep -n '^|[-: |]*|$' gastify/.kdbp/LEDGER.md` → zero separator rows in the whole file. Live read-only run: `kdbp_snapshot` on gastify returns the row above. Battery: every fixture table is well-formed, so the "is this really a header" question is UNPINNED.
findings.fix: Same one-function change as F2: require `re.match(r'^\s*\|[\s:|-]+\|\s*$', lines[i+1])` before accepting a header. Prototyped: gastify's ledger then reads `last: []` (honest-empty) instead of a fabricated row; tests/gabe-kdbp stays 38/38. Ideally also give `ledger`/`pending` a `reason` when no table is found rather than an empty list.

findings.claim: The `cases_for` corpus assert is vacuous — Python's `and`/`or` precedence makes it `(A and B and C) or D`, and D is always true on the fixture, so nothing about `max_cid_in_map` is pinned.
findings.failure_scenario: `ok(d and d["max_cid_in_map"] == 8 and d["corpus"]["next_cid_floor"] is None or d["corpus"].get("max_cid_seen") is None, …)`. The fixture's test files carry no C-id tokens, so `max_cid_seen is None` is True and the disjunction short-circuits to PASS regardless of the left side. Mutating tools.py:569 to `out["max_cid_in_map"] = None` — which breaks map-spec §5.6's `max_cid_in_map from case_home` and the REUSE-before-NEW workflow that /gabe-red depends on — leaves the battery at 89 passed, 0 failed.
findings.evidence: Mutation run: copied skills/gabe-map/scripts to a temp dir, replaced tools.py:569 `out["max_cid_in_map"] = maxmap or None` with `= None`, ran with SERVER_OVERRIDE → `gabe-map battery: 89 passed, 0 failed`. Same result as the unmutated baseline.
findings.fix: Parenthesize and split into two asserts: `ok(d["max_cid_in_map"] == 8, …)` and `ok(d["corpus"]["max_cid_seen"] is None and d["corpus"]["next_cid_floor"] is None, …)`. Then add a fixture test file containing a real C-id (e.g. `def test_thing_C12():`) so `next_cid_floor == 13` is pinned too.

findings.claim: `review_drift` silently accepts unknown subject names, producing `{"subjects": {}, "not_run": []}` — which reads as "everything ran, nothing found", the exact law the tool exists to prevent.
findings.failure_scenario: `mcp__gabe-map__review_drift {"base":"HEAD~1","subjects":["reachh"]}` (a typo, or a stale subject name after a rename) → the answer carries `subjects: {}` and `not_run: []`. /gabe-review's Step 3.4 reads that as five clean deterministic subjects and prices no drift, when in fact zero subjects ran.
findings.evidence: tools_wave2.py:386 `want = set(want) if isinstance(want, list) else None`; :397-398 `def run(name): return want is None or name in want`; :464 `out["not_run"] = [k for k, v in subj.items() if not v.get("ran")]` — an empty `subj` yields an empty `not_run`. Live read-only run against gustify returned `{'subjects': {}, 'not_run': []}`. Contradicts map-spec §5.8's "every subject is {ran, …} or {ran:false, reason}, not_run[] lists them — 'no findings' can never mean 'could not run'". Battery pins only the no-`subjects` call (checks.py:400-402), so the filter path is UNPINNED.
findings.fix: Validate against the known set at :386 — `unknown = set(want) - SUBJECTS`; raise `mq.MapStop("subjects must be a subset of …")` when non-empty. Cheaper alternative: seed `subj` with `{name: {"ran": False, "reason": "not requested"}}` for every unrequested subject so `not_run` is never silently empty.

findings.claim: `who_calls direction=out` still returns a fully-formed `- **Reach:** … (graft@sha)` record line built from CALLEES, not from the callers reach the Reach record is defined as.
findings.failure_scenario: `who_calls {"symbol":"thing","direction":"out","depth":"all"}` returns `reach_line: "- **Reach:** apps/api/other.py · apps/api/services/downstream.py · apps/api/services/thing.py (graft@026983c)"` — the callee set unioned with the grep hits. The line is paste-ready and stamped, so /gabe-red or /gabe-execute can write a callee-derived Reach record into PLAN.md. `review_drift`'s `reach` subject (tools_wave2.py:419-428) and /gabe-review's REACH DRIFT then price `unreached`/`unused_reach` against a record that never described callers.
findings.evidence: tools.py:451 sets `transitive`, :470-471 correctly suppresses the emit for transitive/callee queries and names why, but :473 emits `reach_line` unconditionally. Reproduced on the battery fixture with the fake graft and a `graft/` dir present: output above, `map_claim: present`, `direction: out`. checks.py:404 pins direction/callees/emitted/emit_skipped for this call but never `reach_line`.
findings.fix: At :473, emit the record only for the semantics it names: `out["reach_line"] = mq.reach_line(res, root) if not transitive else None`, with a note mirroring :471. Add the assert beside checks.py:404.

findings.claim: `center_overview`'s `web` block takes the branch chosen by `isinstance(stats.web.unmatched, int)`, but the emitter always writes `unmatched` as a LIST — so screens, fetch_sites and matched are dropped from every real orientation answer.
findings.failure_scenario: On gustify, `mcp__gabe-map__center_overview` returns `web: {"unmatched": 2}` while the committed c4-graph carries `screens: 32, fetch_sites: 54, matched: 52, dynamic: 4, extractor: 'apiFetch'`. An agent orienting with the tool that map-spec §5.8 bills as "graft_repo_map's equivalent" cannot see whether the web arm covered 2 screens or 32 — the dict-comprehension branch written to report exactly that is unreachable against any real emitter output.
findings.evidence: tools_wave2.py:172-173: `"web": {k: … for k in ("screens","fetch_sites","matched","unmatched") …} if isinstance((st.get("web") or {}).get("unmatched"), int) else {"unmatched": len(… or [])}`. Read-only check of gustify's docs/site/center/c4-graph.json: `stats.web.unmatched` is a `list` of length 2 (CLAUDE.md's own contract — "unmatched named, never dropped"). Live call returned `web: {'unmatched': 2}`. The battery fixture also uses a list (checks.py:153 `"web": {"present": True, "unmatched": []}`), so the int branch is dead in the battery too.
findings.fix: Drop the ternary: always report the scalar keys and length-normalize unmatched — `w = st.get("web") or {}; out["web"] = {k: w.get(k) for k in ("screens","fetch_sites","matched") if w.get(k) is not None} | {"unmatched": len(w.get("unmatched") or []) if isinstance(w.get("unmatched"), list) else w.get("unmatched")}`. Assert `web["screens"] == 1` on the fixture.

findings.claim: `map_diff` caps each per-entity list at 20 but computes `more` against 40, so between 21 and 40 added/removed items are dropped with `more: 0` — a silent cap, violating map-spec §5's "every list is capped and the cap is NAMED".
findings.failure_scenario: Two refs apart by a regen that adds 25 endpoints to one entity: `map_diff` reports `endpoints: {"added": [<20 names>], "removed": [], "more": max(0, 25+0-40) = 0}`. Five endpoints vanish from the answer and the result explicitly says nothing more exists — the reader concludes the regen added exactly 20.
findings.evidence: tools_wave2.py:330-332: `add, rem = sorted(...)`, then `d[k] = {"added": add[:20], "removed": rem[:20], "more": max(0, len(add) + len(rem) - 40)}`. The whole `regenerated: True` body (:321-339) is UNPINNED — checks.py:395 pins only `regenerated:false` and :397 only the missing-ref reason. Mutation proof: replacing :329 `for k in ("endpoints","models","schemas","files"):` with `for k in ():` leaves the battery at 89 passed, 0 failed.
findings.fix: `"more": max(0, len(add) - 20) + max(0, len(rem) - 20)` (or reuse `mq.cap_list` so the `+N more (cap N)` string is produced by the one helper). Pin the regenerated path with a fixture that commits a second archmap.

findings.claim: `find` crashes with a raw ValueError on a non-integer `limit` instead of returning the `{stop}` message map-spec §3 requires for bad input.
findings.failure_scenario: `mcp__gabe-map__find {"query":"pantry","limit":"all"}` → `isError:true` with `{"tool":"find","error":"ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'all'"}`. The model gets a Python traceback class name rather than the self-correcting stop text every other bad-input path produces (`detail must be brief | full | raw`, `query must be at least 2 characters`, `kind must be one of …`).
findings.evidence: tools_wave2.py:66 `limit = max(1, min(int(args.get("limit") or 20), mq.CAP))` — unguarded `int()`. Live read-only run against gustify returned the error above. Battery pins the query-length stop (checks.py:378) and the map_census kind stop (:393) but never a bad `limit`.
findings.fix: Wrap: `try: limit = max(1, min(int(args.get("limit") or 20), mq.CAP)) except (TypeError, ValueError): raise mq.MapStop("limit must be an integer (1–%d)" % mq.CAP)`.

findings.claim: The binding contract still describes a seven-tool server in three places, and kdbp-spec §6 claims a battery pin that does not exist.
findings.failure_scenario: A future session reads map-spec.md ("SKILL.md is the lean core; this file binds") to decide what the server must expose, sees "as seven tools" (:10), "the discovery surface is therefore the seven NAMES" (:35) and "`tools/list` (7 names, object schemas, annotations)" (:189), and either trims the registry or writes a battery assert for 7 — contradicting checks.py:238, which pins exactly 15. Separately, kdbp-spec.md:92 lists "verify_commands a/b/none" among the battery's pins; tests/gabe-kdbp/checks.py covers only source a (:213) and source b (:233), so a change that breaks the `none` answer is invisible.
findings.evidence: map-spec.md:10, :35, :189 vs skills/gabe-map/SKILL.md:3/:20/:24/:59 (which correctly say fifteen) and tests/gabe-map/checks.py:238 `set(names) == V1 | W2 and len(names) == 15`. kdbp-spec.md:92 vs tests/gabe-kdbp/checks.py (no `source: none` case). The doctor's parity invariants cover version numbers and skill counts, not spec prose, so neither drift is machine-visible.
findings.fix: Replace "seven tools"/"seven NAMES"/"7 names" with fifteen in map-spec.md:10, :35, :189. Either add a `verify_commands` case in a repo with no BEHAVIOR binding and no manifests (asserting `source` starts with `none:`) or strike "/none" from kdbp-spec.md:92.

findings.claim: `freshness` computes `dirty_map` from the `git diff` output but guards it with the return code of the later `git status` call — a shadowed `rc` that can suppress the "uncommitted regen" state.
findings.failure_scenario: `git status --porcelain` fails (rc != 0 — e.g. an index.lock held by a concurrent commit) while `git diff --name-only <base>` succeeded and lists a modified archmap.json. `dirty_map` evaluates to False, so an in-flight regen is reported as `freshness: "fresh"` / `stale: false` instead of `"uncommitted regen"` / `stale: null`, and untracked files are silently missing from the changed set as well.
findings.evidence: mapquery.py:250 `rc, diff, _ = sh([... "diff", "--name-only", base])`; :253 `rc, st, _ = sh([... "status", "--porcelain", ...])` rebinds `rc`; :261 `dirty_map = any(l.strip().endswith("archmap.json") for l in diff.splitlines()) if rc == 0 else False` reads the status rc against the diff output. The "uncommitted regen" branch (:262-263) is also UNPINNED — mutating `if dirty_map:` to `if False:` leaves the battery at 89 passed, 0 failed (checks.py:280-284 sets an unknown head first, which returns early at :233-235 before this code runs).
findings.fix: Use separate names — `rc_diff, diff, _ = sh(...)` at :250 and `rc_st, st, _ = sh(...)` at :253 — and guard :261 with `rc_diff == 0`. Pin it: modify archmap.json in the fixture worktree without changing `head` and assert `freshness == "uncommitted regen"` and `stale is None`.
